Pakistan's Department of Archaeology and Museums gives Daber Kot at 30.083333, 68.683333 (about 40 km from the stored point, which lies near the centre of Duki district), but no second independent source prints a point for the mound: the Wikipedia heritage list only says 18 km northeast of Duki Town, which contradicts the DOAM point, so the point is held for the owner.

The entry is the collective group of the more than 200 dolmens scattered over central-northern Sardinia (Luras, Mores, Macomer, Buddusò, Dorgali and others); no source gives one point for the group, and the stored point near Sedilo matches no named monument, so no two sources can be quoted for the site's point.

The Harrow Way is a linear prehistoric trackway said to run from Seaton in Devon to Dover in Kent (its western section ending at Farnham); neither Wikipedia nor Wikidata gives it a point, and no source prints coordinates for a centre or main monument, so no two independent sources can be quoted for a point.

Only the Megalithic Portal gives a point for the Tayata site (17.35 N, 97.57 W, flagged as scaled from a bad map), and the stored point is a copy of it; the other pages found give the villages of Santa Cruz and Santa Catarina Tayata, not the site, so no second independent source can be quoted.

The Neolithic settlement lies on the south flank of Cape Apostolos Andreas, about 4 km north of the monastery, so the stored point (about 33 km to the south-west) is wrong. The only source printing a point for the site itself is GeoNames 19283 (Kastros, archaeological/prehistoric site, 35.69442, 34.58590); Wikipedia and Wikidata carry no coordinates, and no second independent source (Pleiades, Megalithic Portal, OSM) gives the site's point, so the point is held for the owner.

The two sources that give a point disagree by about 4 km: the 2024 Frontiers in Microbiology paper (after Dias et al. 1984) prints 16° 17′ 38″ S 46° 44′ 35″ W (about 1.2 km from the stored point), while the GPS-sourced OpenStreetMap cave-entrance node tagged with this Wikidata item is at -16.2584615, -46.7407304 (about 2.8 km away); Wikidata and Wikipedia carry no coordinates, so no two independent sources agree on the site's point.

The Roman Emperors Route is a modern tourism and archaeology project, a 600 km route linking separate Roman sites across Serbia (Sirmium, Singidunum, Viminacium, Felix Romuliana, Naissus/Mediana and others). Neither Wikipedia nor its Wikidata item (no P625) gives a point, and a route of that length has no single centre; the stored point is simply Belgrade. No two sources give the site's point.
